name: SONiC (Software for Open Networking in the Cloud)
what_it_is: SONiC is a free and open-source network operating system based on Linux that runs on vendor-agnostic switches and ASICs. It uses a modular Docker container architecture where each network function runs in its own container, and has been production-hardened in large cloud-provider data centers.
components: SwSS container (Switch State Service — orchagent, portsyncd, neighsyncd)
Platform/hardware abstraction layer (SAI — Switch Abstraction Interface)
measurement: Interface counters and statistics via CLI (show interfaces counters)
BGP neighbor status and prefix counts (show bgp summary)
SNMP polling via dedicated SNMP container
gNMI/gRPC streaming telemetry via telemetry container
PFC watchdog metrics for RDMA/RoCE congestion detection
System status checks (show system-memory, show processes)
configuration: JSON-based configuration files (config_db.json loaded into Redis)
Redis CONFIG_DB as central runtime configuration store
YANG models for structured configuration validation
Minigraph XML for datacenter-style topology configuration
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework documented in the repository
Container restart/isolation can simulate individual service failures (docker restart <container>)
ASIC simulation via virtual switch (vs) platform for testing without real hardware
modes: ONIE installation mode (production deployment on bare-metal switches)
Virtual switch (vs) mode — software simulation for development and testing
Docker-based development environment (build and run without physical ASIC)
VM/KVM mode for learning and integration testing
constraints: Requires Switch Abstraction Interface (SAI) implementation from the ASIC vendor — not all hardware is supported
Master coordination repository only; actual component source code lives in separate sub-repositories (sonic-buildimage, sonic-swss, sonic-frr, etc.) which must be checked out individually
Redis DATABASE container is a single point of coordination — all containers depend on it for state
Virtual switch mode does not emulate full ASIC forwarding performance or all ASIC-specific features
Configuration changes to hardware-forwarding paths require syncd/SAI round-trip, introducing latency compared to software-only stacks
docker_services: database — Redis instance serving as central CONFIG_DB, APPL_DB, ASIC_DB, COUNTERS_DB
swss — Switch State Service (orchagent, portsyncd, neighsyncd, intfmgrd)
syncd — ASIC synchronization daemon bridging SwSS and SAI/hardware
notable_absences: No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering framework
No integrated load/traffic generation tool — requires external tools (e.g., ixia, trex, pktgen)
No GUI or web dashboard in the base repository
Detailed per-platform hardware support matrix is not in this repo (lives in sonic-buildimage)
No native CI/CD pipeline definition in this coordination repository
